newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian domestic credits 3.8 pct down in March.
newsitem.headline: Romanian domestic credits 3.8 pct down in March.

text.p: Romania's internal credits fell by 3.8 percent to 40.3 trillion lei in March, after February's 13.9 percent rise, with non-government credits 6.1 percent down due to higher lending rates, central bank data (BNR) showed.

Tough monetary policies aimed to fight rising inflation, which hit a record high of 30.7 percent in March, have sent up the average lending rates to 112.6 percent in March from 50.8 percent in the New Year, BNR data showed.

Net credits to Romania's government rose by 15.3 percent to 5.2 trillion lei at end-March, when State Treasury General Account posted a 191.5 billion lei deficit against a surplus of 254.3 billion the previous month.
Hard currency loans declined to 18.5 trillion lei in March from 20.55 trillion the previous month, taking about 53 percent of end-March non-government loans.

Leu credits fell slightly to 16.58 trillion lei in March from 16.79 trillion the previous month. Short-term loans accounted for 81 percent of end-March leu credits, of which state companies took about 55 percent. ($=7,092 lei)
